card.line: Bashan was a rich region east of the Jordan River, ruled by King Og, that Israel took and gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

moments.title: Israel defeats King Og
moments.text: Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to fight Israel at Edrei. The LORD told Moses not to fear, and Israel struck Og's army down and took his land.

moments.title: Sixty cities taken
moments.text: Israel captured all sixty cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan, in the region of Argob. Not one city was left untaken, though they had high walls, gates, and bars.

moments.title: Og, last of the Rephaim
moments.text: Og king of Bashan was the only one left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His iron bed was nine cubits long and four cubits wide.

moments.title: Land given to Manasseh
moments.text: Moses gave all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half-tribe of Manasseh. Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the region of Argob and renamed Bashan Havvoth-jair.

moments.title: Golan, a city of refuge
moments.text: Moses set aside three cities east of the Jordan where a person could flee after killing a neighbor unintentionally, with no prior malice. Golan in Bashan was one of them.
